issues.body: In run_case, `$JSCPD` is intentionally expanded unquoted so the default string `npx --yes jscpd@4.0.5` splits into command arguments. ShellCheck reports this construction as SC2086 (word splitting/globbing). The workflow's preceding `shellcheck scripts/tests/test_docs_duplication.sh` step has no exclusion or directive, so the docs-duplication job fails at static analysis and never runs the fixture suite. This also makes the advertised `JSCPD="node …/jscpd"` override depend on unsafe shell parsing.
issues.fix_hint: Represent the command as an array and invoke it as `"${JSCPD_CMD[@]}"`, with a separate safe override mechanism if needed (for example, accept the executable path separately from fixed arguments). Then run the exact workflow shellcheck command and the behavioral self-test.
issues.title: Mandatory shellcheck rejects the unquoted JSCPD command expansion

verdict.summary: The gate is not merge-ready because its mandatory shellcheck step is expected to reject the self-test itself. The script deliberately stores a multi-word command in JSCPD and expands it unquoted; that is precisely the unsafe pattern diagnosed by ShellCheck SC2086. Since the workflow runs shellcheck before the behavioral fixtures, the new hard-gate job will fail before reaching them. Round 1 reported no findings, so this newly identified major finding makes progress regressing.
